findings.title: Materials' 119% earnings hope looks stretched
findings.body: Materials trades at 17.32x forward but 38.01x trailing, a 51-point percentile gap between the two lenses. The forward multiple is priced for 119 percent earnings growth, yet the sector sits at only the 40th percentile of its own five-year range — the market is not treating that growth as a sure thing.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' forward discount is a bet
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward P/E of 19.72 sits at the 35th percentile while its trailing multiple of 28.38 is at the 84th. That 49-point percentile gap implies analysts expect 44 percent earnings growth to rescue a sector that has been richly valued on reported earnings — a sharp re-rating that is far from guaranteed.

findings.title: Information Technology's percentile gap signals caution
findings.body: Information Technology's forward P/E of 21.80 is at the 12th percentile, but its trailing P/E of 37.09 sits at the 56th. The 44-point gap means the market is paying up for 70 percent expected earnings growth, yet the forward multiple's low percentile suggests buyers are not confident enough to push it higher — a disconnect between hope and conviction.
